chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās ibn Ma‘rūf, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Īsā, from Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, who said:

I said to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: What is the least that suffices of tasbih in the salat (prayer)? He said: Three tasbihat, uttered deliberately and unhurriedly; you say: “Subḥān Allāh, Subḥān Allāh, Subḥān Allāh.”
And the second possibility is that we interpret the latter reports as referring to merit and recommendation, not obligation and requirement. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

key_terms.أَخَفُّ: the least or lightest amount that suffices
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: glorification of Allah by saying words such as “Subḥān Allāh”
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: additional merit beyond the minimum requirement
key_terms.مُتَرَسِّلًا: recited calmly, distinctly, and without haste

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tasbih that suffices in rukū‘ and sujūd during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report states the minimum tasbih in salat (prayer), specifically in the context of rukū‘ and sujūd, as three utterances of “Subḥān Allāh” said in a measured manner. The closing phrase indicates a juristic reconciliation in which other reports are understood as recommending additional remembrance rather than making it obligatory.
